summary: Vasily Seseman was a philosopher who studied at Saint Petersburg State University from 1903 to 1909. He later held positions at Saint Petersburg State University (~1915–1919), Vytautas Magnus University (~1923–1940), and Vilnius University (~1940–1950).

Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, completing his PhD at the University of Bonn in 1930. He held posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and served as a professor at the University of Delhi (1959).

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi worked in Indology and history/archaeology, holding degrees from Deccan College and the University of Mumbai. He served as Principal of Morris College and Vidarbha Institute, and later as Honorary Professor at Nagpur University (1957–1966).

Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala worked in Indology and history/archaeology, studying at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow. He served as Curator of the Government Museum, Mathura (1931), Director of Lucknow's State Museum (1940), and with the Archaeological Survey of India.

Vasudha Dalmia is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who earned degrees from Miranda House, Cologne, JNU, and Heidelberg. Her appointments include the University of Tübingen, the University of California, Berkeley, and Yale University.

Vasudha Narayanan works in religious studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Madras, University of Mumbai, and Harvard University. She became Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida (~1982) and served as President of the AAR.

Vasumati Karandikar is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied at the University of Mumbai (M.A. 2017–2019, 2022–2024) and earned a Ph.D. in 2021 from Kavikulaguru Kalidas Sanskrit University, where she was also a student.

Vatroslav Jagić was a linguist who studied under Franz Xaver Miklosich, August Leskien, and Albrecht Weber, earning a PhD from Leipzig. He held professorships at Odesa University, Humboldt University of Berlin, Saint Petersburg State University, and the University of Vienna.

Vedprakash Sharma works in Indology. He studied at the University of Delhi (1980–1985) and earned a Ph.D. from Maharshi Dayanand University (2005–2008), later working as a Research Associate at the University of Delhi.

Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi works in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields, having studied under Manikya Shastri and Martanda Dikshit. He held positions at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha, the French Institute of Pondicherry, Jagadguru Ramanandacharya Rajasthan Sanskrit University, and Karnataka Samskrit University.

Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indology scholar who earned degrees from Sir C. R. Reddy College, Andhra University, and Osmania University. He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1971 and served as a visiting professor at Chicago and Emory.

Velizar Sadovski works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (1996–2001), where he became Universitätsdozent in 2001, and joined the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1998.

Vempati Kutumba Sastry is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University (2003–2008) and was president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (~2006–2018).

Ven. Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhante Dhammasakkaro and K. L. Dhammajoti. He completed degrees through the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Hong Kong (PhD).

Venoth Nallisamy is an Indology scholar who earned degrees from Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Open University Malaysia, and a PhD from the University of Malaya. In 2024, he became a Senior Lecturer at INTI International University.

Vera Aleksandrovna Novikova was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov and Aleksandr Semënovič Zimin. She later worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts and Saint Petersburg State University.

Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge. She held research and teaching posts at St Edmund's College, St Hilda's College, Oxford, and King's College London before joining Yale University in 2006.

Verrier Elwin worked in Indology and history/archaeology, having studied at Dean Close School and Merton College. He served as Deputy-Director of the Anthropological Survey of India (1946–1949) and Adviser for Tribal Affairs in the North-East Frontier Agency (1954).

Vesna Wallace is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed her doctorate at the University of California, Berkeley. She held the Numata Chair at the University of Oxford and holds a professorship at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Vicente Fatone was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Calcutta (1937–1938). He held professorships at the National University of the Litoral, the National University of La Plata, and the University of Buenos Aires.
